items.title: CMake installs resource files that do not exist in the repository

findings.title: CMake installs resource files that do not exist in the repository
findings.explanation: Directory listing of DBS_STN/Resources/nets shows only 3.obj, cent_detect_hist.pkl, detect_mask.pkl, mer_pca_mesh.pkl, shape_hist.pkl, shape_pcas.pkl, stn_shape_mask.pkl and transformer_classifier_test.pt; net_transformer.pt is absent (read_file returned 'No such file'). Likewise STNSegmenter/CMakeLists.txt:18,23 list Resources/MNI/MNI152_T1_1mm_brain.nii.gz and Resources/nets/cent_pred.pt, which are also absent. CMake install of missing files fails the extension build/package step.
findings.suggestion: Either commit the referenced weights/templates or remove them from MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES and rely on the existing download path (STNSegmenter.py:730).

items.title: Wheel downloaded from a Box.com shared link and installed without integrity check

findings.title: Wheel downloaded from a Box.com shared link and installed without integrity check
findings.explanation: On Linux/Python 3.12 the module fetches a binary wheel from an anonymous file-sharing link and pip-installs it into Slicer's Python (line 44). The link is not a package index, has no checksum or signature verification, and the content can be replaced by whoever controls the Box share, giving arbitrary code execution in the user's Slicer session. It also runs at import time (see the try/except at lines 55-62).
findings.suggestion: Install antspyx from PyPI (or a pinned, hash-verified release asset) and only after explicit user confirmation; never install binaries from file-sharing links.

findings.title: Binary wheel downloaded from a third-party file host and installed
findings.evidence:
download_url = "https://app.box.com/shared/static/mu1gy26t80oopbtv3mndl5yveb6s4431.whl"
        whl_filename = "antspyx-0.6.2-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl"
        whl_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / whl_filename

        logging.info("Downloading antspyx wheel from %s", download_url)
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(download_url, str(whl_path))
findings.explanation: On a specific Linux/Python combination, _install_antspyx() fetches a wheel from app.box.com with no checksum, then installs it. Anyone who can replace the Box file controls code that runs in the user's Slicer Python. The URL is also a personal share link that can change.
findings.suggestion: Install antspyx from PyPI with a pinned version, or verify a SHA256 of the wheel before installing. Do not depend on a personal file-share link.

items.title: Code installed directly from a git branch at import time

findings.title: Code installed directly from a git branch at import time
findings.explanation: pip installs the current tip of an unpinned third-party branch into Slicer's environment; whatever is committed there later executes inside Slicer. The same call is repeated in _install_segm_runtime_dependencies (line 189). No revision pin, no user confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Depend on a released, version-pinned package (or a pinned commit) and install it only on explicit user action.

items.title: EXTENSION_DEPENDS does not match the catalog entry's build_dependencies

findings.title: EXTENSION_DEPENDS does not match the catalog entry's build_dependencies
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "SlicerElastix;SlicerNetstim") # AtlasMapping uses Elastix, DBS workflow integrates with Netstim/Lead-OR
findings.explanation: The catalog entry declares "build_dependencies": [], so the index will not fetch SlicerElastix/SlicerNetstim before building, while AtlasMapping.py:1027 imports Elastix at runtime and DBS_STN integrates with Netstim. The two declarations must agree for the entry to be mechanically usable.
findings.suggestion: Add SlicerElastix and SlicerNetstim to build_dependencies in the catalog entry (or drop them from EXTENSION_DEPENDS if truly optional).

findings.title: Catalog build_dependencies does not match EXTENSION_DEPENDS
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "SlicerElastix;SlicerNetstim") # AtlasMapping uses Elastix, DBS workflow integrates with Netstim/Lead-OR
findings.explanation: CMakeLists.txt declares EXTENSION_DEPENDS of SlicerElastix and SlicerNetstim, but the catalog entry lists no build_dependencies. The index build may not see the dependencies, and the policy requires them to match.
findings.suggestion: Align the catalog entry's build_dependencies with EXTENSION_DEPENDS (and add SlicerPyTorch once the torch install is moved to PyTorchUtils).

items.title: Loop over an integer raises TypeError

findings.title: Iteration over an integer in compute_distances_to_mesh
findings.explanation: shape[0] is an int, so this raises TypeError whenever the function is called; the function also mixes numpy and torch operands. It is dead/broken code in the shift-prediction path.
findings.suggestion: Use range(points_to_compute.shape[0]) and convert operands consistently.

findings.title: Loop over an integer raises TypeError
findings.explanation: compute_distances_to_mesh iterates over points_to_compute.shape[0], which is an int. The first call raises TypeError, so the function cannot run. It is a visible correctness bug.
findings.suggestion: Use range(points_to_compute.shape[0]) or remove the function if it is unused.

items.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity check and loaded with torch.load

findings.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity check and loaded with torch.load
findings.explanation: shp_pred.pt is downloaded from a GitHub release with no checksum, then passed to torch.load, which unpickles arbitrary code. Anyone able to replace the release asset, or a man-in-the-middle, can execute code on the user's machine. A corrupt download also triggers a re-download and a second load. The first load also runs with no weights_only restriction.
findings.suggestion: Verify a pinned SHA256 for each downloaded or bundled .pt file before loading. Load with torch.load(..., weights_only=True) or use safetensors. Document the source of the weights.

items.title: Multiple packages installed at import without asking the user

findings.title: Multiple packages installed at import without asking the user
findings.explanation: dbs-pure-lib, antspyx, intensity-normalization, scikit-learn and pandas are all installed silently at import (STNSegmenter.py:22,52,75,122,186-189; DBSShiftPrediction.py:9,37,46; segm_lib/visualisiation.py:51). These installs modify the shared Slicer Python for all users and can pull transitive dependencies that conflict with Slicer's bundled numpy/scipy.
findings.suggestion: Move dependency installation behind an explicit user prompt (slicer.util.pip_install after confirmation) or declare them as extension dependencies.

items.title: Automatic package installation at import time

findings.title: torch.load of downloaded weights without weights_only
findings.explanation: Weights are auto-downloaded from GitHub releases (line 730) and then unpickled with torch.load; on torch versions before 2.6 this can execute arbitrary code from the file. The same pattern is at lines 178 and DBSShiftPrediction.py:1761. Files are also loaded from the module resource directory, which is writable by the user.
findings.suggestion: Pass weights_only=True (or load a safetensors file) and verify a published SHA256 of the downloaded weights.

findings.title: Automatic package installation at import time
findings.explanation: Multiple modules automatically run `slicer.util.pip_install(...)` at import time (top-level module loading / when modules are accessed), installing third-party packages without user consent. Slicer extensions must not perform automatic package installations at import time or startup.
findings.suggestion: Remove automatic pip installation of external packages at module import time.

findings.title: Package installs at import time, including unpinned GitHub installs
findings.explanation: STNSegmenter.py installs packages when the module is loaded (dbs-pure-lib, antspyx, a git+https ANTsTorch install, intensity-normalization). Each install runs without a version pin or user confirmation, and the ANTsTorch install follows a moving default branch. Module import can therefore change the shared Python environment.
findings.suggestion: Move installs behind an explicit user action in the widget, pin versions, and avoid installing from a VCS URL. Install only on first use of the feature, not at import.

items.title: PyTorch installed with pip at module import instead of via PyTorchUtils

findings.title: PyTorch installed with pip at module import instead of via PyTorchUtils
findings.explanation: Scripted modules are imported when Slicer loads the extension, so this runs for every user who installs DBSCoalignment, even if they never open STNSegmenter. It pulls a PyPI torch build (CPU/CUDA mismatch, large download, no user confirmation) into Slicer's shared Python and can break other extensions; the same pattern is at DBSShiftPrediction.py:17-25 and STNSegmenter.py:1745-1750 (torchio).
findings.suggestion: Remove the import-time installs and use the Slicer PyTorch extension's PyTorchUtils (add PyTorch to build_dependencies and EXTENSION_DEPENDS), prompting the user before any download.

findings.title: PyTorch installed directly via pip instead of PyTorchUtils
findings.explanation: The extension installs PyTorch directly via `slicer.util.pip_install('torch')` inside module files (`STNSegmenter/STNSegmenter.py` and `DBS_STN/DBSShiftPrediction.py`) rather than declaring `PyTorchUtils` in `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` and using it correctly according to Slicer guidelines. This can disrupt Slicer's shared Python environment and cause package version conflicts.
findings.suggestion: Remove direct `pip_install('torch')` calls and declare PyTorchUtils as an extension dependency in CMakeLists.txt and the catalog entry.

findings.title: PyTorch installed via pip_install instead of the PyTorch extension
findings.explanation: Torch is installed with slicer.util.pip_install('torch') at import time and in logic construction. This bypasses SlicerPyTorch and can change or conflict with the Python environment that Slicer and other extensions use, including for users who never open the module. The policy requires torch to come through PyTorchUtils.
findings.suggestion: Add SlicerPyTorch to EXTENSION_DEPENDS and build_dependencies, and use the PyTorchUtils install logic instead of pip_install('torch'). Remove the same call from STNSegmenter/STNSegmenter.py line 70 and line 189.

items.title: Bundled model weights and MNI template have no documented license or provenance

findings.title: Bundled model weights and MNI template have no documented license or provenance
findings.evidence:
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2025 Czech Technical University in Prague, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
findings.explanation: The extension code is MIT, but the repository ships trained networks (transformer_classifier_test.pt, shape_pcas.pkl, mer_pca_mesh.pkl, 3.obj) and MNI152-derived templates whose origin, training data and redistribution terms are not stated; MNI templates carry their own attribution terms. Users cannot tell what they may redistribute.
findings.suggestion: Add a NOTICE/Resources README stating the source, license and training data of each bundled model and template.

findings.title: Bundled model weights and MNI template lack stated terms
findings.evidence:
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2025 Czech Technical University in Prague
findings.explanation: The repository license covers the code only. The pretrained .pt/.pkl networks and the MNI152 template are bundled and downloaded without stated terms or attribution. Distribution is probably permitted, but the terms are not documented.
findings.suggestion: Document the source and license of the model weights and the MNI template, and include attribution where required.

items.title: Module metadata and help text are still template placeholders

findings.title: Module metadata and help text are still template placeholders
findings.evidence:
self.parent.contributors = [
            "John Doe (AnyWare Corp.)"]  # TODO: replace with "Firstname Lastname (Organization)"
findings.explanation: Contributors, help text and acknowledgement are the Slicer template defaults ('This is an example of scripted loadable module bundled in an extension'), so users get no in-application guidance for a neurosurgical workflow; the same applies to AtlasMapping.py:238-248, LabelConversion.py:49 and TextToMarkups.py:61.
findings.suggestion: Fill in real contributors, help text and acknowledgements, and add a research-use disclaimer.

items.title: Module test calls process() with the wrong signature

findings.title: Module test calls process() with the wrong signature
findings.explanation: AtlasMappingLogic.process is defined as process(self, inputMesh, inputBaseTransform) (line 866-868), so the bundled test raises TypeError immediately; the test also treats a model node as a volume (inputMesh.GetImageData()). The test therefore cannot validate anything.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite the test against the real signature and a real input mesh/transform, or remove it.

findings.title: Test calls process() with the wrong signature
findings.explanation: The AtlasMapping test calls logic.process with four arguments and checks volume scalar ranges, but process() takes (inputMesh, inputBaseTransform) and returns a transform. The test would fail if enabled, and it is not part of the build test list.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite the test for the current process() API, or remove the stale test code.

items.title: No clinical or research-use disclaimer and no tests

findings.title: No clinical or research-use disclaimer and no tests
findings.evidence:
Project: SlicerDBSCoalignment

This project focuses on improving the precision of electrode placement in Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery
findings.explanation: The software supports surgical electrode placement, but the README and CMake metadata contain no statement that results are research-only and not for clinical decisions. Test suites are commented out (e.g., DBS_STN/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt), so there is no regression coverage.
findings.suggestion: Add a research-use disclaimer, document model provenance and validation for the networks, and enable at least a smoke test.

items.title: Resource directories present in the repo are not installed by CMake

findings.title: Resource directories present in the repo are not installed by CMake
findings.explanation: DBS_STN/Resources/MNI/MNI152_T1_1mm_subbr_mask.nii.gz, Resources/elastix/*.txt, Resources/Smk_utils/*.smk and Resources/py/bet.py exist in the repository but are not listed in MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES, so they will not be present in an installed extension. Whether the runtime code needs them was not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add the resources actually used at runtime to MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES, or delete the unused ones.

items.title: Shell-like command built by string formatting and shlex.split

findings.title: Shell-like command built by string formatting and shlex.split
findings.explanation: register_t2_to_t1 and _run_cli_wm_segmentation build commands by f-string and shlex.split. Paths with spaces or quotes break, and an embedded quote can alter the Python command passed to 'python -c'. Inputs are user-selected paths, so this is a robustness issue more than a remote attack, but it is still fragile.
findings.suggestion: Pass arguments as a list without a shell, and call the Python APIs directly rather than building python -c strings.

items.title: Temporary working directories are intentionally never cleaned up

findings.title: Temporary working directories are intentionally never cleaned up
findings.evidence:
# Keep temporary output available for troubleshooting.
            # Set cleanup() here once diagnostics are no longer needed.
            pass
findings.explanation: Every AtlasMapping run leaves a TemporaryDirectory (line 882) with NIfTI volumes, distance maps and elastix logs on disk; the object is garbage collected without cleanup, so repeated use accumulates hundreds of MB in the user's temp folder.
findings.suggestion: Call working_dir_obj.cleanup() in the finally block, optionally keeping the log text in the error message only.

items.title: WM segmentation uses Python `or` on numpy arrays

findings.title: WM segmentation uses Python `or` on numpy arrays
findings.explanation: `si == 3` is an array, so `or` raises 'truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous' and the WM mask step fails. The same bug is in DBS_STN/Lib/slicer_preprocessing.py:33. Additionally `subprocess.check_output(cmd, env={})` at line 38 runs the child with an empty environment, which will typically fail.
findings.suggestion: Use np.isin(si, (3, 4, 5)) and pass a proper environment to the subprocess.

items.title: nibabel installed on demand inside a helper function

findings.title: nibabel installed on demand inside a helper function
findings.explanation: A silent pip install into Slicer's shared environment triggered by a helper call, without user confirmation; nibabel is also installed at import in STNSegmenter.py:187.
findings.suggestion: Declare nibabel as a dependency and install it once, with user confirmation.

items.title: pickle.load of bundled .pkl resources

findings.title: pickle.load of bundled .pkl resources
findings.explanation: Model/histogram pickles are deserialized with pickle (also DBSShiftPrediction.py:1038). The files ship with the extension so the risk is limited, but pickle can execute code if a resource file is replaced, and the provenance of these pickles is undocumented.
findings.suggestion: Prefer a non-executable format (npz/json) or document and checksum the pickle files.

findings.title: Pickle deserialization of bundled model and atlas files
findings.explanation: Several .pkl files are read with pickle.load (DBS_STN/DBSShiftPrediction.py line 1036-1040 and STNSegmenter line 104-108). The files ship inside the extension, so the risk is limited to tampering with the package or the user's copy. The same code path is still unsafe in principle.
findings.suggestion: Convert the bundled pickles to a non-executable format (JSON/NPZ) or document their provenance and hashes.

items.title: No automated tests are registered

findings.title: No automated tests are registered
findings.explanation: All five Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt files have the test registration commented out, so the extension's CI provides no functional coverage; combined with the broken AtlasMapping test this means nothing is verified automatically.
findings.suggestion: Register at least a smoke test per module.

items.title: Personal local path committed in AGENTS.md

findings.title: Personal local path committed in AGENTS.md
findings.explanation: A developer's Windows user path is committed in the repository. It is not a credential and contains no instructions to reviewers, but it is environment-specific clutter that should not ship.
findings.suggestion: Remove the machine-specific path from AGENTS.md.
